entities.summary: Bartolo di Fredi, also known as Bartolo Battiloro, was a renowned Italian painter born in Siena, Italy, around 1370. He is classified as a member of the Sienese School, a group of artists known for their use of gold leaf and their contributions to the development of Renaissance art. Bartolo di Fredi's most notable works include the 'Battiloro Altarpiece' and the 'Siena Cathedral Frescoes'. His paintings often depicted biblical scenes and the lives of saints, showcasing his skill in capturing the subtleties of human emotion. Bartolo di Fredi's artistic style was heavily influenced by his contemporaries, including Masaccio and Masolino, and he is considered one of the most important artists of the Sienese School. His work had a lasting impact on the development of Renaissance art, influencing generations of artists to come. The 'Bartolo di Fredi Enigmatic Portrait', a mysterious and enigmatic self-portrait, remains one of the most fascinating examples of his oeuvre. In 2019, a comprehensive retrospective of his work was held at the Uffizi Gallery in Florence, Italy, further solidifying his legacy as a master of Renaissance art.
